title: Humans Are Closer to T-Rex Than T-Rex Was to Stegosaurus
provenance: Owner priority-override run (2026-10-02), topic from data/topic_history.jsonl's queued set (score 93, id t_humans_are_closer_to_t_rex_than_t_rex_wa). Source-checked live against Wikipedia (no web-search API in this session; see bench/ab/topic_trex_source_check.md).

claims.claim: Tyrannosaurus rex lived from about 69 to 66 million years ago, at the very end of the Cretaceous period.
Stegosaurus lived from about 155 to 145 million years ago, in the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages of the Jurassic.
The gap in time between the last Stegosaurus and the first Tyrannosaurus rex is roughly 76 to 89 million years.

Tyrannosaurus rex went extinct about 66 million years ago, and modern humans are a recent species on that timescale — so T. rex is separated from modern humans by less time than it is separated from Stegosaurus. Do not state a precise 'modern humans appeared X years ago' figure; the claim only needs the human lineage to be far closer to the present than 66 million years, not an exact date.
claims.source_hint: Wikipedia: Homo sapiens (human origins placed at 'several million years ago' at most for the broader hominin lineage, far closer to the present than 66 Mya)

honesty_note: Use the ranges, not invented single numbers: T. rex 69-66 Mya, Stegosaurus 155-145 Mya. Do not claim an exact 'humans appeared N years ago' figure beyond what's needed for the comparison.
